questions.stem: What does the y-axis represent on an energy level diagram?
questions.explanation: The y-axis on an energy level diagram represents energy. The x-axis represents the progress of the reaction. The diagram shows the relative energy levels of the reactants and products.

questions.stem: On an energy level diagram, if the products line is lower than the reactants line, the reaction is:
questions.explanation: If the products are at a lower energy level than the reactants, energy has been released to the surroundings. This is an exothermic reaction. The energy difference between reactants and products is the enthalpy change (ΔH).

questions.stem: What does the arrow labelled ΔH represent on an energy level diagram?

options.text: The overall energy change (enthalpy change) of the reaction

questions.explanation: ΔH (delta H) represents the overall enthalpy change of the reaction. It is the difference in energy between the reactants and products. A downward arrow indicates exothermic (ΔH negative); an upward arrow indicates endothermic (ΔH positive).

questions.stem: An energy level diagram shows reactants at 200 kJ and products at 350 kJ. What is the enthalpy change?
questions.explanation: ΔH = energy of products - energy of reactants = 350 - 200 = +150 kJ. Since the products have more energy than the reactants, the reaction is endothermic and ΔH is positive.

questions.stem: Which key feature must always be labelled on a complete energy level diagram?

options.text: The names of the catalysts used
Reactants, products, and the enthalpy change (ΔH)

questions.explanation: A complete energy level diagram must label the energy levels of the reactants and products, and show the enthalpy change (ΔH) with an arrow between them. The axes (energy and progress of reaction) should also be labelled.

questions.stem: In an exothermic reaction, where is more energy stored?

options.text: In the surroundings before the reaction
Equal amounts in reactants and products

questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, the reactants have more stored energy than the products. The difference in energy is released to the surroundings as heat, which is why the products are shown at a lower energy level on the diagram.

questions.stem: A reaction has ΔH = -285 kJ/mol. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The reaction is exothermic and releases 285 kJ per mole
The reaction does not involve any energy change
The products have more energy than the reactants
The reaction is endothermic and absorbs 285 kJ per mole

questions.explanation: A negative ΔH means the reaction is exothermic. The reaction releases 285 kJ of energy per mole to the surroundings. The products have less energy than the reactants, and the difference (285 kJ) is transferred to the surroundings.
